title: Browser webGpu RL Clone with some *gadgets*
author: _javas_crypt
selftext:
**Title:**  
I started this as an AI-generated Rocket League experiment. Somehow it now has a controllable crash-test dummy.  
A couple of weeks ago I started a small experiment: how far can I get building a Rocket League-style game for the browser while heavily using AI for development?  
The first version was honestly exactly what you’d expect — a rough little Rocket League clone. A car, a ball, an arena, some physics and a lot of things that were *technically working* but didn’t necessarily feel like a real game yet.  
I kept working on it, fixing the physics, controls, presentation and all the small things that make the difference between “AI generated demo” and something you can actually sit down and play.  
At some point the project started moving away from simply trying to recreate Rocket League.  
And that’s where **Carambolage Mode** came from.  
The main feature I’m currently having the most fun with is the **dummy**. It isn’t just a physics object getting thrown around — **you can actually control it yourself**.  
So instead of the player experience ending with the car physics, you suddenly have this second completely different kind of character to mess around with inside the same physics sandbox. Combined with the cars, ball and arena it creates exactly the kind of stupid emergent situations I like in physics games.  
Current features include:  
full browser-based 3D game  
driveable cars  
ball physics  
goals and scoring  
boost  
Rocket League-inspired arena/gameplay  
HUD / match UI  
**Carambolage Mode**  
physics-driven dummy  
**directly controllable dummy**  
interactions between the dummy, cars and the rest of the physics world  
several weeks of continuous iteration from the original AI prototype rather than a one-shot generated demo  
The funny part is that the project originally wasn’t supposed to become much more than an experiment. My first videos were basically “*look what GPT-6/Astra managed to generate*”.  
Then it became “*okay, this is actually becoming playable*”.  
And now I’m at the point where I’m adding completely new mechanics instead of just trying to imitate Rocket League.  
That’s probably the part of AI-assisted game development I find most interesting: getting the initial prototype is easy. Turning that prototype into something with its **own mechanics and identity** is where the actual project starts.  
You can play the current build directly in your browser here:  
**https://lucasgeorg1–overtime-game-web.eu-west.modal.run**  
I’d especially be interested in feedback on **Carambolage Mode and the controllable dummy** — whether the movement feels fun, what you’d do with the mechanic, and how far you’d push the whole car + ragdoll/character physics idea.  
It’s still very much an evolving project, so breaking things is absolutely allowed. :)
